newsitem.title: CHINA: GOLD CLOSES HIGHER BUT OFF DAY'S PEAK IN HONG KONG.
newsitem.headline: GOLD CLOSES HIGHER BUT OFF DAY'S PEAK IN HONG KONG.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed higher but off the day's peak on short-covering, recovering after New York's slide overnight, dealers said on Wednesday.
Bullion rose to an intraday high of US$328.60/329.10 an ounce before it closed at US$328.50/329.00, against New York's price around US$327.10 on Tuesday.
"The market players were short-covering, believing that gold had seen its lowest point and was recovering," a dealer at a major bank said.
"The market is very nervous and there is no news to support the gold price," a dealer said.
"Most traders are unsure of where the market is turning next, and they are watching U.S. dollar movements," he said.
Dealers said gold would range-trade between US$320 and $330 in the short-term.
Local gold ended HK$13 higher at HK$3,039 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -4.00 from its previous fix at -5.50.
